0.text:
The process is initiated by a Player who wants to start character creation. Following this, two activities begin in parallel. The first is for the Player to come up with good character names. The second parallel activity is for the Player to check for a battle.net account. If an account does not exist, the Player enters their account information and then clicks a confirmation link in their email. If an account already exists, this step is skipped.

Next, the Player checks for an active WoW subscription. If a subscription is not active, the Player must select a payment method. If the chosen method is credit card, they enter their credit card information. If the chosen method is direct debit, they enter their IBAN and BIC numbers. Once the payment information is entered, or if a subscription was already active, the Player logs into the game and selects a realm, race, and class.

After both the account and subscription checks are complete and the Player has come up with character names, the two parallel paths merge. The Player then enters a name for their character. A check is performed to see if the name is available. If the name is not available, the Player must enter a different name and the check is repeated. If the name is available, the Blizzard System sends a confirmation and selfies to the Player. This communication triggers the release of an expansion, after which the Blizzard System sends an expansion release message, and the process concludes with the character having been created.

0.text: The process for an Applicant begins with the need to work and live in Austria. At the same time, the applicant organizes their accommodation and bank account, and also checks the visa requirements. Once both of these are complete, the applicant gathers the required documents, determines the competent representation office, and then submits the visa application. The visa application is sent to the Austrian Authority's representation office, which then reviews the application. A decision is made on whether the application is valid. If the application is valid, the authority issues the visa, and the process ends with the visa process being complete. If the application is not valid, the process ends with the application being refused.

1.text: The process for an applicant begins with the need to work and live in Austria. First, the applicant must organize accommodation and a bank account, after which they gather the required documents. A check is then performed to see if additional documents are requested. If they are, the applicant must gather the required documents again. If no additional documents are needed, the applicant identifies the competent representation office. Next, the visa type is determined. Whether it is a Schengen Visa (A/C) or a National Visa (D), the applicant then submits the visa application. This application is sent to the Austrian Authorities, where the representation office will receive and process it. Once processing is complete, the process ends with the visa being obtained.

If the repair was successful, the User sends a review or video, and the process concludes with the repair completed and reviewed. If the repair did not work, the User sends the device to an expert, and the process ends.

0.text: The process begins for a Parent when they start planning their maternity leave. First, they fetch information about potential models and then select a model. After the model is selected, the parent collects the relevant information. Following this, two notifications are sent out in parallel: one to Social Security and another to the Company. Once both notifications have been completed, the parent gathers information from the companies. Next, a decision is made about whether to extend the leave. If the decision is to extend the leave, the parent goes back to collect relevant information again. If the decision is not to extend the leave, the process concludes with the parenting plan being finalized.

After this, two notifications are sent out in parallel. The Parent notifies Social Security, which in turn processes the notification. At the same time, the Parent notifies their Company, which then gathers information and sends it back to the Parent. Once both notifications are complete, the process waits for the leave period to pass. After the leave period, the Parent decides about an extension. If they decide not to extend, the process ends as the leave period ends. If they decide to extend, the process concludes with the leave period being extended.

This model describes four separate processes for handling accidents based on the insured person's status.

In the case of Insured Employment, the process begins when an incident occurs to an employee. The employee informs their employer of the incident by sending an incident report. The employer then assesses the accident's severity. Following the assessment, if there is a fatality or serious injury, the employer reports to the Labour Inspectorate. Concurrently, if the employee is killed or unable to work for more than three days, the employer also reports to the Accident Insurance Provider. Once these reports are made, the process concludes.

For a Self-Employed person, the process starts when an accident occurs. The self-employed person then reports to the Accident Insurance Provider, after which the process ends.

In an Education context, the process starts when an accident occurs to a student or schoolchild. The student reports the accident to the directorate by sending an accident report. The school or university then reports to the Accident Insurance Provider, and the process ends.

For a Private Insurance holder, the process begins when an accident occurs to the insured party. The insured party reports the accident to their private insurance. A check is then made to determine if it was a fatality. If it was not a fatality, the process ends. If it was a fatality, the insured party reports the fatality to the private insurance, and then the process ends.
